judge.evidence_requirement: For every expectation and dimension, quote or reference specific output evidence. A disposition label without its artifact-specific reason is not evidence.

dimensions.description: Checks quoted output evidence that authority follows host policy, requirements, scoped repository instructions, mechanical configuration, nearby practice, and labelled fallback in that order while retaining conflicts.
Checks quoted output evidence that every compact concern has exactly one artifact-specific disposition and that dispositions are not presented as defects.
Checks quoted output evidence that missing inputs and specialist capability remain unresolved gaps with routes instead of invented context or shallow specialist advice.
Checks quoted output evidence that the response advises without authoring a design, mutating artifacts, executing validation, creating Review findings, or taking over caller operations.
Checks quoted output evidence that tiny work receives compact coverage while complex or conflicted work retains enough detail to be actionable.

evals.name: tiny TypeScript change under sparse authority
evals.prompt: Assess this proposed change, not its prose: in src/format-id.ts, replace a local two-line lowercase helper with String.prototype.toLowerCase(). Intent: preserve current identifier output. Scope: that function only. Current artifact: a three-line TypeScript patch. Applicable authority: the user requires no behavior change; the repository has no instruction file, formatter, linter, tests, or nearby equivalent. Activity: implementation. Return Engineering concern coverage. Do not change files or run commands.
evals.expected_output: Compact coverage keeps missing repository evidence visible, uses fallback only where needed, disposes every concern once, and identifies proof conditions without running them.
expectations: Every concern has exactly one applicable-now, applicable-later, or justified not-applicable disposition tied to this tiny patch.
Absent repository authority remains a gap rather than invented local policy.
Fallback guidance is labelled and limited to uncovered applicable-now concerns.
The response identifies behavior-preservation evidence without running validation.
The amount of guidance is proportionate to a tiny change and prompt cost is considered.
Sampled human review checks that semantic advice remains useful under alternate wording.

evals.name: architectural proposal with nested conflicting authority
evals.prompt: Assess an existing service-boundary proposal. Intent: move invoice retry ownership from the API process to the queue worker. Scope: services/api/retry and services/worker/invoice only. Current artifact: proposal revision r17. Authority, high to low: organization policy requires retries to avoid duplicate charges; the ticket requires worker ownership; root AGENTS.md says all external effects use adapters; services/worker/AGENTS.md requires queue handlers to be idempotent; compiler config enforces strict null checks; a nearby old worker performs charges directly and retries without an idempotency key. Activity: design. Keep all conflicts visible. Do not write a replacement design.
evals.expected_output: Coverage applies nested authority by scope and precedence, treats the old pattern as descriptive and conflicting, and advises on the proposal without choosing or writing the design.
expectations: Authority resolution preserves organization policy, requirement intent, root and nested repository scope, mechanical configuration, and nearby practice in order.
The direct-charge retry pattern remains visible as pre-existing bad practice and does not override stronger authority.
Every concern has exactly one current disposition with an artifact-specific reason.
Advice identifies relevant ownership, contracts, state, failure, compatibility, and evidence questions without authoring a replacement architecture.
Conflicts and unresolved effects remain explicit.
Sampled human review checks semantic correctness and useful restraint.

evals.name: non-code CI change with weak authority and specialist gap
evals.prompt: Assess a proposed YAML-only CI change that adds a performance budget before deployment. Intent: detect a p95 regression. Scope: .github/workflows/deploy.yml. Current artifact: draft workflow revision ci-4. Authority: the ticket says deployments must stop on material regression; nearby jobs use inconsistent thresholds; no performance owner, approved threshold, workload model, or specialist Skill is available. Activity: design. Do not invent a threshold, edit YAML, or run the workflow.
evals.expected_output: Coverage treats the technical non-code artifact as assessable, preserves weak authority and missing performance expertise, and routes the caller instead of inventing specialist criteria.
expectations: The YAML workflow is treated as a technical non-code artifact, not excluded as generic non-code work.
Inconsistent nearby thresholds remain weak descriptive evidence.
Missing threshold authority, workload model, and performance capability remain unresolved gaps.
The response gives a performance specialist route without imitating performance expertise.
Every concern has one justified current disposition and no validation is run.
Sampled human review checks that the route and gaps are actionable.

evals.name: review activity preserves independent disagreement
evals.prompt: Assess immutable range a1b2..c3d4 during review. Intent: cache product permissions without changing authorization results. Scope: packages/auth/cache.js and its tests. Current artifact: the immutable diff. Authority: organization policy requires deny-by-default; the ticket permits caching; repository tests require cache invalidation after role changes. The implementation handoff claims state-and-invariants is not applicable, while the fresh reviewer says invalidation state is applicable now. Activity: review. Provide concern coverage, not Review findings or severity.
evals.expected_output: Fresh coverage resolves authority from the immutable review artifact, keeps the implementation claim and reviewer disagreement visible, and does not convert concern dispositions into findings.
expectations: Review resolves fresh concern coverage from the immutable range rather than inheriting the handoff conclusion.
The state-and-invariants disagreement remains visible with its authority basis.
Every concern has one disposition and dispositions are not defects or Review findings.
The response avoids severity, finding confidence, fix direction, and review coordination.
Deny-by-default remains higher authority than the ticket and implementation claim.
Sampled human review checks independence and semantic authority handling.
